title: Chameleon
text:
Police inspector Ochumelov was crossing the market square in a new greatcoat when he heard a shout. A crowd had gathered around Khryukin, a goldsmith, who was holding up a bleeding finger. A small white puppy, trembling, sat on the ground nearby. The dog had bitten him.

Ochumelov took charge. He declared that dogs running loose would no longer be tolerated, that the owner would be fined and the animal destroyed. Then someone in the crowd said it looked like General Zhigalov's dog. Ochumelov suddenly felt hot, asked for help taking off his coat, and announced that Khryukin must have provoked the little thing, probably by jabbing a cigarette in its face.

A policeman then said the general had only pointer dogs. Ochumelov changed his mind again: this was a mongrel, a stray, and it should be put down. The policeman had second thoughts, and the inspector, now cold, put his coat back on and called the dog a delicate thoroughbred. This went back and forth until the general's cook happened by. The dog was not the general's, he said, but belonged to the general's brother, who had just come for a visit.

Ochumelov beamed, called the puppy a lively little thing, and let the cook take it. The crowd laughed at Khryukin, and Ochumelov, threatening the goldsmith that he would deal with him later, wrapped himself in his coat and walked on.
lesson: If your judgment of a case changes when you learn who is involved, you are not judging the case. Decide on the facts first, then find out whose interests are at stake.
people: Police inspector Ochumelov, Khryukin the goldsmith, a policeman, the general's cook
